Information in nerve cells is carried by changes in a cell’s membrane potential. The change in membrane potential ranges from approximately -70 to +30 mV. Membrane potential is measured by placing an electrode inside a cell. For detailed information exchange, it is necessary to connect individual cells and electrodes. In operation of the neural interface, cell death caused by the connection between cells and electrodes is a problem. Solving this problem will dramatically increase the performance of the neural interface. To solve the problem, not only must the electrode shape be optimized but also the technology for the connection between cells and electrodes should be optimized. We discovered a method that is less likely to induce cell death and has a high rate of successful cell membrane perforation, and applied it to microelectrodes. We made a microelectrode to which this method was applied. We used this electrode for two types of cells, PC12 and ND7/23 cells, and here we describe the data we obtained.

articleTitle: Characteristic Cracking Pattern Generated on Tissue Slice as a Useful Index for Medical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Although biopsy is one of the most important methods for diagnosis in diseases, there exists undesired ambiguity judged through the information obtained from the visual inspection of tissue slices. Here, we report that, with a simple treatment by use of a urethane sheet, characteristic cracking pattern is generated for tissue slices depending on the difference of disease state. We used the tissue slices obtained from mouse liver with different stages of disease: Healthy normal state, Simple steatosis, Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis and Hepatocellular carcinoma. It is suggested that the cracking pattern of a tissue slice caused by absorbing provides useful information for distinguishing among the disease states.

articleTitle: In-Situ Observation of Fracture Behavior of Silicon in a Transmission Electron Microscope
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This study reports a combinational method of tensile testing with TEM observation to observe the local area in a large magnified view. Our target material is single-crystal silicon that behaves in a brittle manner under tension until fracture in general. We developed a novel silicon chip for tensile testing of nanoscale silicon film with compliant mechanism for maintaining the observation point on the tensile specimen. The experimental results showed crack initiation and then incredibly crack shielding in single-crystal silicon under tensile loading.

articleTitle: Body Parts Estimation for Motion Capture System Using Multiple Depth Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Capturing the motion is important in various scenes. Several types of motion capture systems such as optical or inertial type have been developed so far. These type motion capturing systems can capture the high precise motion. But these type motion capture systems need to attach the markers or some devices and disturb the natural motion. On the other hand, there are marker less motion capture methods by using RGB or depth sensor such as Microsoft Kinect. These methods can get the motion capture data without attachment of devices, but these methods cannot get the motion capture data in occlusion regions of sensor. To resolve the problem, we have developed a motion capture system with multiple depth sensors. At first, the system gets the multiple depth data and combines them by unifying the coordinate systems. Then, the system estimates which part of the body each point in the combined point cloud by the Random Forest. Finally, the system estimates the joint positions from the body parts. This paper proposes the method of body parts estimation for the proposed motion capture system and compares the accuracy of estimation among the features for Random Forests.

articleTitle: Force-visualization based Sensing System Facilitates Medical Operation in Deep Area
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Haptic information is less at endoscopic surgery and the development of force or haptic sense for the surgery is demanded. With this in mind, our group have developed several force haptic sensing systems based on force-visualization mechanisms. The benefits of the systems involve the absence of electrical components, disposability, easy sterilization/disinfection, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) compatibility, and low cost. Here, we introduce the developed systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Bayesian Tracker for Various Condition using Thermal Infrared Imagery
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Self-driving car has the capability to navigate autonomously with high awareness of the surrounding environment. They have an intelligent method to avoid collision and predict movements of other objects. One of the key technology in order to achieve this level of safety is object tracking. Accurate and quick vision-based method compete to increase the reliability. Several tracking methods utilized visible spectrum camera to gather data. However, there are challenges that arise, especially in minimal lighting such as cloudy and rainy conditions or at night. To overcome this problem, we use thermal image. We propose a newly enhanced Smoothing Stochastic Approximate Monte Carlo (SSAMC) based tracker with unique preprocessing Gamma Normalization and Median Filter. We tested our tracker in self-driving car theme data from Linköping Thermal InfraRed (LTIR). This data is captured from both a moving and a static sensor, both have different difficulty level. The experiment results show that the tracker achieved a better result compared to other methods. We achieved an accuracy of 0.8786 with a higher frame per second computation time of 4.6405.

articleTitle: Tongue Training Robot Development for Swallowing Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In the field of swallowing rehabilitation, tongue exercise training can be applied to maintain and recover tongue function. Nevertheless, securing sufficient training time is difficult because few speech-language-hearing therapists can administer such training. Therefore, we developed a tongue training robot for swallowing rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Development of a Precision-grip based Interface for 4-DoF Articulated Forceps
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we develop a user interface for multi degree-of-freedom (DoF) articulated forceps intended for minimally invasive transnasal endoscopic neurosurgery. This user interface intuitively and precisely controls the multiple DoFs of the forceps tip through a pen-type linkage held by the thumb and the forefinger in a similar way to the dexterous handwriting motion, while the forceps position and orientation are controlled by the handpalm motion over a parallel link mechanism. We evaluate the feasibility of the proposed user interface on an object manipulation experiment and a suturing experiment. In an additional experiment, a surgeon successfully performed simulated dural suture on surgical glove material using multi-DoF articulated forceps with the proposed interface.

articleTitle: Cooperative movement in grasping and development of grasping-training robot
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In previous research, we designed a grasp-training robot for the post-stroke patient in relation to its usability and wearability for ease of use in clinical practice. Experimental results obtained from a post-stroke patient showed that by combining a grasping support of the robot and the mechanism for pushing an elastic bar on the palm, the grasping reflex was induced in paralyzed patient in a clinical test that involves measuring EMG signals. However, the robot has one structural issue that subjects could not use the robot without fixing subjects' wrist joint, then the robot could not realize synergistic movement of the wrist and the fingers. In this paper, we introduced the new mechanism that can extend the wrist joint into the previous robot having the glove type device. New mechanism is designed by imitating a mechanism of the bascule bridge. We introduced the wire drive system having one motor and the stepped shaft for pulling wires. As the shaft has steps, the shaft can pull different amount of wires for the glove type device and the wrist movement mechanism, then the robot can realize the extension of the wrist and the flexion of the fingers as a cooperative motion.

articleTitle: Multimodal Measurement of Cell Culture Conditions Using Hydrogel Culture Substrate having Fluorescence Microsensors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We proposed multimodal measurement for spatiotemporal monitoring interactions between cells and environment using hydrogel substrate having fluorescence sensor pillars. We measured local change of [Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>] and pH and demonstrated the culture of the osteoblast precursor cell on the hydrogel surface.

articleTitle: Basic research on micro processing characteristics of reverse lift-off process
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In micro electromechanical systems(MEMS) technology, lift-off processes are general patterning methods for the formation of amorphous alloy thick film structures. However, thicknesses of structures fabricated in this method are not uniform and cross-sectional shapes are not flat because sputtered particles are blocked by the sidewalls of the lift-off layer. In order to solve this problem, a reverse lift-off process is proposed as a new patterning method <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. In the reverse lift-off process, the desired structure is formed on the top of the convex pattern such as the substrate. In contrast to the lift-off process, the thickness of the structure is uniform and the cross-sectional shape is rectangular because sputtered particles are not blocked by the sidewalls. In this research, thick film structures were fabricated in reverse lift-off processes from the width of the convex pattern on the order of micrometers. And the film thickness and the cross-sectional shape of the fabricated structure are measured, and the micro processing characteristics of the reverse lift-off process, which had not yet been elucidated, were investigated. This demonstrates the usefulness of fabricating the thick film micro structures in the reverse lift-off process.

articleTitle: Robotic Microscope System for Studying the Basic Principles of Brain Function
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper reports the development of robotic microscope system to understand the basic principles of brain function through the rigorous and integrated studies of worm's nerve activity and behavior. By using the system, we revealed that, during olfactory navigation, worms compute time-differential and time-integral of odor concentration for decision-making. We also revealed the genes required for the neural computations, whose counterparts in humans also known to play important roles in the brain. Thus, the mechanisms revealed in worms will help us understand how our own brain works.

articleTitle: Microscopic laser interferometry to measure the displacement of micromechanical objects
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper proposed a method to measure the displacement of micromechanical components moving on the focal plane of optical microscopy. This method is based on the interferometric analysis using the laser system and the grating fabricated on the micromechanical components. The advantage of this method is its high measurement speed, accuracy and the simplicity of the configuration. We demonstrated to measure the displacement of oscillatory body at the speed of 50 kHz and within the noise of 35 nm. This method will be a promising option to measure and control the translational motion of the micromechanical devices at high frequency domain.

articleTitle: Clinical neuro-mechanics for design and analysis of motor assistive devices
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we present some of our works on development and analysis of motion assist devices for patients with lower limb motor paralysis due to central nervous system disorder. We think that the assistive devices should provide assistance according to the human nervous system's structure and mechanism of controlling motions, and as well their evaluation should be based on it. Here we present our results of evaluation of the pre-post changes of patients with paretic lower limbs after stroke or myelopathy who underwent motor function recovery using HAL, and development of new ways of controlling HAL and of a new mobility device to assist sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit postural transitions.

articleTitle: Aggregation of Charged Microgels by Relatively Diamagnetic Assembly
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we suggest a three-dimensional fabricating method with biocompatible microgels by using relatively diamagnetic assembly. Microgels were charged positively or negatively before assembly. These microgels attracted each other, whereby an aggregate was constructed. Furthermore, an aggregate hard to disperse after transferring to a dish was obtained by mixing the same amounts of positive microgels 490 nm in diameter and negative microgels 2400 nm in diameter. This result shows that the modeling method is one of the most promising approaches for biocompatible three-dimensional printing.

articleTitle: Estimation of Bound Water Ratio in Extracellular Matrices using Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) can be effective evaluation method of tissue-engineered (TE) cartilage. As initial stage, we measured gelatin gel as a simple model of cartilage by THz-TDS and estimated the bound water ratio in gelatin gel by dielectric relaxation study.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Fabrication of Microneedle Array for Transdermal Ion Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: More than 22,000 people were taken to hospital and nearly 100 people were killed due to heat waves across Japan in this summer. Hence, there is a high demand to detect the risk of heat stroke before it strikes. The minimally invasive insertion of needles offers considerable advantages over the conventional sensing routes. Moreover sensing at transdermal region is easily accessible without any complications. Measurement of electrolyte abnormalities resulting from prolonged sweating would be easiest way to detect the heatstroke risk. In this regard, we proposed a low cost, facile preparation, easy to use enzyme free sensor for the detection of ions in transdermal region. Microneedles was achieved by replicating structures from a laser engraved stainless steel master. And then PDMS elastomer was poured on stainless steel master, cured for 2 hours at 70°C and peeled off. The peeled off microneedle array structure is semi flexible and transparent. Then, Au/Ti electrodes were deposited on PDMS using shadow mask to make electrodes for sensing studies. Finally the electrodes were modified using Ag/AgCl and ZnO for sensing characterizations. Electrochemical studies were performed using the conventional three electrode system by employing electrochemical workstation (Bipotentiosrat 2325, ALS Japan). Cyclic voltammetric and amperometric techniques were used for electrochemical analysis of the bare and metal oxide functionalized microneedle electrodes in the range of 10-100 μM. To improve the selectivity of the sensor, the interference studies will be carried out using uric acid, glucose and dopamine. Finally, examination in in vitro animal studies is scheduled.

articleTitle: Optimized Convolutional Gabor Using Particle Swarm Optimization : Case Study: Vehicle Classification Tasks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: The increase of data is becoming faster, so the amount of data becomes very large, which in the end creates a big data problem. Three aspects that are often identified as problems faced with big data are volume, velocity, and variety. In this paper, the big data problem that will be solved is the problem of volume, which is quantity/ amount of data. Several common methods for solving the problem are compressing the data, reducing the dimensionality feature, and managing the workflow storage. This paper applies the Particle Swarm optimization, an evolutionary algorithm, in dimensionality feature reduction. The case study used in this paper is image data with classification task. We exhibit the framework by applying particle swarm optimization algorithm in the reduction feature. In practice, such frameworks can not only be done for data images but can be used for other data with classification task. This paper compares the performance with and without feature selection. From the results of the comparison, feature selection achieves a better accuracy and a faster computation time.

articleTitle: Intraoral pH Measurement: A Cool Way to Recognize Stress
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In recent years, mental disorders has become serious problem caused by excessive stress. Globally more than 60% of workers are testified to be in stress during work hours. The common diagnostic tools for measuring stress are an electroencephalogram (EEG), body temperature, an electrocardiogram (ECG) and self-questionnaire. Though thee measurement techniques are sensitive enough to identify stress, they are quite complex and poorly suitable for point of care (POC) testing. In addition, salivary alpha amylase measurement is commonly used for stress evaluation. However, it's unsuitable for continuous measurement of the enzyme activity. Fortunately there is a link between the pH and stress levels of the body. Therefore in this study we aim to continuously monitor the pH fluctuation in an oral cavity using mouthpiece pH sensor. Although, electrolyte free Ag/AgIO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> reference electrode method facilitated us to make the miniaturized pH sensor. Initially for calibration experiments were done using standard pH buffer solutions (pH4.01, pH5.00, pH6.00 and pH7,01) using Ag/AgIO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> reference electrode and antimony (Sb) electrode supplied by Chemical Equipment Co., Ltd. (Part Number M 20 E 16002). The observed sensor response is shown in Figure 1 and the sensitivity was around -58.433 mV/pH. Then the electrodes were attached to the mouthpiece device and measured the real time pH fluctuation in mouth by applying noise induced stress. The measurement procedure was at first both electrodes were immersed in a buffer solution for 5 mins, then hearing white noise and finally when no noise is heard. The stress load and non-stress load measurement result is shown in Figure 2. A standard solution voltage values were taken for conversion factor for pH. When no stress load is applied the measurement, there is no serious fluctuation was observed in pH values. On the other hand during white noise hearing, the pH was significantly decreases than the normal value. Hence it is proved that stress levels directly affected the pH values of the saliva. More investigation is underway for conformation.

articleTitle: Extended Flow Reduction Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we present a high-resolution and highspeed micropipette utilizing an extended flow reduction mechanism. The mechanism is based on a microbubble in the microfluidic circuit, which works as a kind of the temporal buffer tank against to the input flow. We evaluated the performances of developed micropipette, and the results showed that the resolution was 2.75 pL and the operation range was up to 500 Hz.

articleTitle: A cellular contractility monitoring system allowing for high-throughput and long-term analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Because of lack of high throughput screening systems for mechanobiological study, genome wide screening for cellular contractility-related genes has not been conducted. To overcome this situation, we developed a cellular contraction assay based on oxygen plasma-treated silicone gel substrate and image processing algorithm. Using our system, we could evaluate which protein or gene mutation contributes to cellular contractility in high-throughput manner.

articleTitle: Verification concerning load distribution for distributed control actuation module
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, in other to evaluate the load distribution, evaluate the load on each active caster when modeling Active Caster system when n basic casters are implemented. In the previous research, the model was just considered statics. If the load actuation modules are concentrate to the center position, the load on each caster is dispersed. On the other hand, if the load is not set to the center of actuation modules, the load for each caster is different. Thus, to avoid the trouble, the load distribution control should be implemented. In order to implement the load distribution control, it is necessary for each caster to know at which position of the actuation module the load is placed. In this paper, we verified the load position and the load on each caster in current model using a simulator.

articleTitle: Analysis of Rockers during the Stance Phase of Gait for Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: As rockers are fundamental components of the walking gait, this study aims to reveal the individual differences in rockers and to examine the factors that cause these differences. We examined the relations among the percent duration of each rocker and important factors, such as age, sex, and the time-averaged floor reaction force (TAFRF). TAFRF has been subdivided into two components: the vertical component and the traveling direction component. We analyzed the gait data of 179 healthy individuals and determined the percent duration of each rocker during the complete stance phase. Individual differences in the percent durations of the ankle and forefoot rocker phases were larger than those in the heel rocker phase. Although, the individual differences in the duration of rocker phases did not correlate with age, a significant difference existed in the percent durations between the males and the females (p <; 0.05). Strong correlations were observed between the percent duration of the ankle rocker and both the TAFRF components. Conversely, the duration of the forefoot rocker phase exhibited a weak correlation with both the TAFRF components. These results indicate that there exist no age-related differences in the use of rockers; however, the sex of an individual does cause significant differences. The high proportion of the ankle rocker phase in the total stance phase is relevant to the high efficiency of locomotion. This study suggests that the percent durations of the ankle and forefoot rocker phases could be a new feature value to assess gait, which would further aid in measuring the health conditions and physical declination of individuals.

articleTitle: An Episodic Memory Model with Slow Features Extraction for Topological Map Building
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper presents a new integration model for on-line topological map building with environment slow features detection. The proposed model is formed by the integration of Bayesian Adaptive Resonance Associative Memory (BARAM) and Incremental Slow Feature Analysis (IncSFA). IncSFA incrementally extracts slowly varying features from a rapidly changing input signal. These slow features will be fed to BARAM for environment learning to build a topological map. The explored environment is represented as a set of neurons (nodes) and edges that connecting all nodes. Each neuron represents a distinct place and edges store robot traverse information that leads the robot to travel from one node to another. The proposed model is an unsupervised learning technique that does not require any prior knowledge of what an environment is supposed to be for ease of implementation. The effectiveness of our proposed method is validated by several standardized benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Patch-type Wireless Forehead Vital Sensing Device
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper reports a wearable vital sensing device towards medical analysis with artificial intelligent. Recently, there have been many researches related to medical analysis with artificial intelligent. Current researches are analysis based on stored data in hospitals. The amount of data for analysis gradually increases according to focusing on the medical analysis. However, depending on the increase, the burden of servers or host computers increase as well. In order to decrease the amount of processing, the concept of “edge computing” is proposed. The optimization of the system on wearable devices is required to realize the concept. Here, in this study, we demonstrate a wearable vital sensing device which detects oxygen level in blood based on a pulse oximeter and heart beat pulse for edge computing.

articleTitle: Evaluation of living tissue model based on force measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: What is needed to create a brain surgery simulator is to create a model for simulation. We are involved in creating models of brain, dura mater and blood vessels in making a brain surgery simulator. In this research, we will evaluate the mechanical properties based on the creation of the dura mater model. Dura mater is a living soft tissue, it consists of intercellular substance and moisture, so dura mater has both elasticity and viscosity. In order to evaluate the mechanical properties of the dura mater, we will measure the viscoelasticity. Then, model evaluation not only from physical property values but also from the viewpoint of force measurement becomes necessary to create a dura mater model.

articleTitle: Strategies of Stable Grasp and Accurate Release for Dual-finger Micromanipulator
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In microscale, adhesion force enables us to grasp targets with only one end-effector. However, due to the vibration of the driving unit and the environmental disturbance, losing target often happens during the grasp. The adhesion also makes releasing the targets from the end-effector difficult, and release accuracy cannot be guaranteed. In this paper, we proposed novel strategies of grasp and release for a dual-finger micromanipulator. The dual-finger micromanipulator includes two micropipettes as the end-effectors. One micropipette is fixed and the other active micropipette is actuated by a piezo-driven 3-DOF parallel mechanism. Tips of the micropipettes are heated to form spherical tips, then the tips are grinded to form hemispherical shapes. The big flat surfaces of the hemispherical end-effectors can increase the success rate of the grasp and avoid the target lose. In the release strategy, the hemispherical tip of the active micropipette is coated with gel to keep the target always sticking on the tip of active micropipette. Then, the active pipette is controlled to vibrate, and release the target adhered on its tip.

articleTitle: Research on walking support method using cooperative cane robots
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper describes a cane-type walk-aid robot for elderly people. Walk is the most fundamental exercise and essential to our life. We developed a robot to replace a commercially available cane that can be used easily by elderlies in their daily life. In this research, two walk-aid robots were used to support walking. The user can use a pair of cane robots by simple operation. As a result of an experiment, it was confirmed that the robots decreased the agitation of the trunk, and it was confirmed that the robots functioned as walk aid

articleTitle: High-speed On-chip Mixing Utilizing Vortex Generation by Ultra-high-speed Local Flow
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We succeeded in high-speed on-chip mixing utilizing on-demand generation of vortex by high-speed flow control. Utilizing on-chip membrane pumps, we can generate the vortex at the local point in a microchannel even in a static flow. Applying this technique to the onchip mixing, the results showed the mixing time of 500 micro-seconds. From the result, we confirmed that we achieved the on-demand high-speed mixing on a chip was achieved.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Control of Cell Culture Microenvironment by Microfluidic Probe Integrated Device
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we developed a novel microfluidic device to control a local chemical stimulation area toward cell-based assays. The device consists of a cell culture channel and MFP channels which have a pair of the injection and aspiration ports installed on the ceiling of the cell culture chamber. The device has been evaluated by a fluidic simulation using Finite Element Method (FEM), and flow control and chemical stimulation experiments on cells. Control of chemical stimulation from several cells to cell population scale can be possible by regulating the flow ratio. The local chemical stimulation area can be estimated by fluidic simulation because the result of the experiment and simulation are identical. The result of cell collection experiment showed that we control the amounts of collecting cells by regulating the flow ratio using the device. We conclude that the device can be powerful tool for biological applications such as the differentiation control of pluripotent stem cells and other cells signaling studies.

articleTitle: Surface Potential Measurement of a Silicon Fast Recovery Diode under Applied Bias Voltages by Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We have measured a semiconductor region of a commercial silicon fast recovery diode (Si-FRD) under applied bias voltages by frequency modulation atomic force microscopy and Kelvin probe force microscopy. Under applied reverse bias voltage, a potential contrast was observed at a pn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> junction in a potential image of the Si-FRD. Under applied forward bias voltage, A potential contrast was observed at a n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>n junction in a potential image of the Si-FRD with a state of conductivity modulation.

articleTitle: Studing Making micro structure with Biodegradable materials
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: For the donor scarcity problem, there are many Tissue Engineering studies. We fabricated toroidal cell structures inside a microfluidic device for tissue engineering applications. A photo-crosslinkable biodegradable hydrogel gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) was employed to encapsulate biological cells for assembling cell structures. stabilizeing the unstable GelMA manufacturing method, we review the manufacturing method and searched for a method that can be stavly produced. So changing the diakysis method, It was possible to prepare GelMA which is suitable as a cell culture medium. RLC-18 cells grow up on the micro structure. articleTitle: Haptic Virtual Fixtures to Assist Endonasal Micro Robotic Surgery through Virtual Reality Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We propose a force feedback algorithm that combines guidance and forbidden region virtual fixtures to enhance the safety in robot assisted endonasal neurosurgery, the concept was tested using virtual reality simulation, and the results from the experiments showed compact tool trajectories with a decrease in the harmful contacts.

abstract: Local analysis of single cells within the cell population is emphasized. In this paper, we developed local environmental control system which could control the chemical stimulus locally at micro-scale by using two micro pipettes. Furthermore, we pointed out the problems in the local environmental control system and improved the system.

articleTitle: Mechanical Characterization of a Single Yeast Cell Using a Robot Integrated Microfluidic Chip
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper reports the evaluation results of Young's modulus of single Yeast cell (BY4741). We compared the Young's modulus of wild type and mutant type (ΔCCW12) using our constructed system. The system consists of a robot integrated microfluidic chip and a microscope with an optical tweezers system. The Young's modulus is measured by compressing the cell and measuring cellular reactive force. We succeeded in measuring wild type cells and mutant cells and compared their difference.

articleTitle: Printed self-oscillatory mechanism inspired by an electric bell
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a printed self-oscillatory mechanism inspired by an electric bell. We have proposed paper mechatronics to make a robot with printing methods. In the paper mechatronics, we also aim to fabricate a controller with printing methods. We attempt to obtain a control signal from a mechanism. An electric bell generates an oscillatory signal with a coupling mechanism between a coil and a magnet. We develop a printed electric bell on a paper with printing methods. We propose the design of the electric bell which can be fabricated on a sheet of paper. The coil and the wiring were printed on the paper, and the device was fabricated by folding the paper. We demonstrate that the device oscillates for 23 min by applying a 0.5 A of constant current. The design is scalable to be applied for microsystems with using printing methods.

articleTitle: Brain signal acquisition methods in BCIs to estimate human motion intention – a survey
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: Brain Computer Interfaces (BCIs) play an important role in current technological era to replace the disrupted neuromuscular pathways of humans caused by disorders or amputation. Especially, in restoring the motor functions of disabled or amputated body parts using wearable robotic devices, BCIs contribute to estimate the user's motion in terms of next motion onset, intended motion, and its velocity to control them. Brain signal acquisition is one of the important steps of a BCI. Over the time, both invasive and non-invasive techniques for signal acquisition are in use. This paper reviews available brain signal acquisition techniques in terms of mutual drawbacks and benefits, current status, challenges, future developments, etc...
